scope: Exactly two genuinely new, non-L14, US-primary scientific/big-physics candidates. This proposal does not modify the ledger, longlist, P4, selection, routing, or state.

binding_interpretation.G1: Two independent current demand sources are required, including a primary buyer/procurement/filing. A future startup feature need not already have its own purchase order, but buyer specifications and funded project activity must be exact-category.
binding_interpretation.G7: Each candidate has a bounded 2026-2029 preparation path, at least two timing sources, a primary/official 2028-2035 project trigger tightly linked to the product, launch TRL, window risk, and a 2034 kill date.
binding_interpretation.source_rule: Each ranked record cites at least 12 accepted-or-acceptance-recommended sources, at least 5 peer-reviewed technical works, at least 3 primary demand validators, a competitor-primary source, and policy/geography evidence. New sources have complete India-origin audits.

decision_summary.recommendation: Advance both to an independent P5 red team. If only one structural repair is required, rank 1 is the stronger choice because its buyer specification is unusually exact and its first experiment is below $100k.

ranked_candidates.concept: Radiation-aware 5 ps timing-integrity daughtercard for EIC-class streaming detectors: clock conditioning, live fiber/board-delay metrology, deterministic power-cycle phase recovery, and bunch-ID continuity in one endpoint
named_buyer_examples: Brookhaven National Laboratory ePIC DAQ/electronics program
DOE accelerator detector collaborations migrating to streaming readout
ranked_candidates.painful_job: ePIC's buyer-side design records require roughly 5 ps clock jitter for timing detectors, 20 ps persistent phase stability, fine-delay monitoring, power-cycle recovery, and a unique bunch-crossing identity. Standard White Rabbit fan-out proves sub-nanosecond distribution, but the detector edge still has board delay, transceiver asymmetry, thermal drift, upset, and restart continuity failure modes that must be measured rather than assumed.
ranked_candidates.product: A radiation-screened FMC/AMC daughtercard and firmware appliance combining a TClink/White-Rabbit-compatible endpoint, dual clock cleaners, loopback TDC, temperature and SFP telemetry, redundant clock-path voting, persistent phase calibration, and a monotonic 64-bit bunch-ID continuity monitor. It exports evidence-grade health records to EPICS without replacing the facility's network or DAQ architecture.
ranked_candidates.frontier_vision: Make picosecond timing an auditable service boundary: every detector partition can prove phase, delay, restart identity, and failover integrity continuously, then extend the same endpoint to free-electron lasers, distributed quantum-network experiments, and telescope arrays.
ranked_candidates.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: reproduce the ePIC clock tree and freeze an open interface around Artix/Kintex-class FPGA and commercial clock cleaners. 2027: build four daughtercards and validate closed-loop board/fiber delay estimation. 2028: temperature-cycle two 10 km paths, execute 100 power cycles and injected link/clock faults, and complete a proton or heavy-ion single-event screen. 2029: place an engineering lot with one ePIC detector subgroup and require a paid qualification or written procurement-path commitment.
ranked_candidates.launch_2030_timing_thesis: The ePIC detailed schedule runs detector electronics, services, integration, procurement, and installation through the 2028-2035 window, while the EIC is funded into construction and targets operations in the early 2030s. A 2030 product enters during final integration, commissioning, spares, and second-source qualification rather than after timing architecture is frozen.
ranked_candidates.demand_trigger_2030_2034: EIC/ePIC detector-electronics integration, clock-distribution qualification, installation, commissioning, and spares procurement during 2030-2034, anchored by BNL's explicit 5 ps jitter/20 ps phase requirements, its 2025 resource-loaded schedule through 2035, and DOE's 2026 CD-3B long-lead funding.
ranked_candidates.competition_outlook_2030: Closest competitors are Safran's WR-Z16 (multi-source White Rabbit fan-out and failover), Instrumentation Technologies' Libera Sync (actively compensated RF clock transfer), CERN's open White Rabbit endpoint/core, and detector teams' custom TClink boards. The non-cosmetic wedge is endpoint-level, radiation-aware, dual-ended phase observability with same-phase power-cycle recovery and bunch-ID continuity; it is not another timing switch or point-to-point RF link.
ranked_candidates.timing_window_risk: ePIC may lock a fully in-house endpoint before 2030, or a clock-cleaner vendor may add enough telemetry that the daughtercard becomes a low-margin integration service. Kill the standalone product if no detector subgroup accepts its interface by end-2028 or if Safran/Libera demonstrates the full detector-edge continuity specification on the target board form factor.
ranked_candidates.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034; earlier commercial kill at end-2029 without a paid qualification or written procurement path
ranked_candidates.extreme_edge: Persistently recover a detector's absolute clock phase within 20 ps across power cycles and keep a 64-bit bunch identity continuous through path failover, turning an otherwise invisible synchronization fault into a bounded, attributable event.
ranked_candidates.first_experiment: 2027-2028, 12 months: four endpoint cards on two 10 km fiber paths; temperature cycle -20 to +50 C, execute 100 cold starts, inject SFP/path/master faults and FPGA configuration upsets, and compare against a metrology-grade reference. Pass only if recovered-clock jitter is <=5 ps RMS, absolute phase stays within 100 ps across temperature, restart phase repeats within 20 ps, failover produces no bunch-ID discontinuity, and all injected faults are localized. Kill on any unrecoverable silent phase slip or if two independent detector engineers reject the interface as unusable.
ranked_candidates.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: A 2028 evaluation with one ePIC timing-detector group followed by a 2029 paid qualification, approved-vendor path, or in-kind procurement work package; absent one of these, do not count engagement.
ranked_candidates.safety_regulatory_export_path: Use low-voltage electronics safety/EMC, DOE laboratory configuration-control and radiation-qualification procedures, and documented FPGA supply-chain provenance. US DOE civilian science is the base case. No cross-border sale is required; any later export is classified and screened before quotation.
ranked_candidates.founder_fit_note: The signal-integrity, FPGA timing, sensor telemetry, embedded control, and automated test work maps directly to generic EE/CE skills; detector radiation assurance and DOE quality documentation require specialist partners.

G1.rationale: Two independent BNL buyer documents state exact 5 ps/20 ps timing needs and board requirements; a third official schedule and DOE CD-3B funding establish active procurement/integration context.

G2.rationale: All five academic works are final journal articles with DOI/publisher evidence; no preprint is used.

G3.rationale: The 12-month $98k four-card experiment has numerical jitter, phase, restart, failover, fault-localization, and buyer-interface kills.

G4.rationale: Safran WR-Z16, Libera Sync, CERN White Rabbit, and custom TClink boards are named; detector-edge continuity and live board/fiber observability are a functional architecture difference, not cosmetic packaging.

G5.rationale: The constituent clock, TDC, delay-correction, and optical-link mechanisms are demonstrated. The experiment directly tests the unproven integration edge.

G6.rationale: US civilian DOE science is the base case; EMC, radiation assurance, configuration control, supply-chain provenance, and later export screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: Preparation is bounded through 2029; BNL's exact timing specification, a 2028-2035 resource-loaded detector schedule, CD-3B funding, early-2030s EIC operation, readiness TRL, incumbent risk, and kill dates are explicit.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: BNL buyer specifications and funded EIC schedule are exact-category.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Auditable picosecond time continuity is a facility-wide control primitive.

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Few buyers, but each facility has many endpoints and high failure cost.

competition_whitespace.evidence: Strong timing vendors exist; the narrow detector-edge continuity layer remains unbundled.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: Every load-bearing metric is observable and fault-injectable.

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: 20 ps same-phase restart/failover is an order tighter than sub-ns fan-out assurance.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Strong US beachhead; no China claim.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: EIC integration and commissioning run through 2030-2034.

expansion_economics.evidence: Same integrity endpoint can serve FELs, quantum networks, and telescope arrays.

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Core work is circuits, FPGA timing, controls, sensing, and test.

ranked_candidates.distinctness_check: New L13 detector-edge timing product; not a relabel of D-19, A-02, A-21, A-22, the E-04 cryogenic interconnect, or any L05 beam/RF-power product.

ranked_candidates.concept: Adaptive SRF field-stability daughtercard: online electromechanical system identification plus safe piezo predistortion for PIP-II/EIC-class low-level RF platforms
named_buyer_examples: Fermilab PIP-II LLRF and SRF teams
Brookhaven National Laboratory EIC RF-controls subsystem
Jefferson Lab SRF-controls and EIC integration teams
ranked_candidates.painful_job: PIP-II's own project report documents Lorentz-force detuning, fast-piezo feedback difficulty, suspected ponderomotive instability, and further calibration before full-gradient operation. EIC is simultaneously migrating more than 100 RF systems to a modular common platform and has ordered initial chassis, leaving a narrow but real socket for a reusable adaptive-control daughtercard.
ranked_candidates.product: An AMC/FMC-compatible deterministic FPGA daughtercard and software pack that identifies each cavity's Lorentz/piezo transfer function online, detects unsafe ponderomotive modes, synthesizes constrained feedforward/piezo waveforms, and records a qualification dossier. It plugs into BNL's Common Platform or MTCA.4 and does not replace the carrier, EPICS, RF front-end, or interlocks.
ranked_candidates.frontier_vision: Turn every narrow-band SRF cavity into a self-characterizing controlled plant, shrinking commissioning from expert tuning campaigns to repeatable qualification and reducing RF overhead across future accelerator fleets.
ranked_candidates.precompany_plan_2026_2029: 2026: implement recursive system identification, constrained piezo feedforward, instability guards, and cavity-emulator regression tests. 2027: demonstrate on 325 and 650 MHz real-time emulators and publish safety bounds. 2028: integrate with one SRF test stand or cryomodule at a US lab through an SBIR/CRADA or paid evaluation. 2029: require a signed daughtercard interface, paid qualification, or procurement work package for EIC/PIP-II commissioning or spares.
ranked_candidates.launch_2030_timing_thesis: PIP-II completes its new SRF linac around 2028 and then enters commissioning/operations for LBNF/DUNE, while EIC construction and RF-controls integration continue into the early 2030s. The card launches into commissioning, repeat-cavity tuning, platform migration, and spares rather than attempting to displace already-selected carriers.
ranked_candidates.demand_trigger_2030_2034: PIP-II commissioning and reliability optimization after its 2028 completion plus EIC integration/commissioning of more than 100 RF systems during 2030-2034. DOE's EIC CD-3B review records ten Common Platform chassis already ordered and continuing RF-control development; BNL's June 2026 cavity test says the next full-system opportunity may be a year or more away while critical components are prepared for tunnel installation.
ranked_candidates.competition_outlook_2030: Closest competitors are BNL/JLab's in-house Common Platform algorithms, Fermilab/SLAC LCLS-II-derived controllers, Instrumentation Technologies' Libera LLRF, KEK's FPGA real-time cavity simulator/control work, and bespoke MTCA.4 cards. The non-cosmetic wedge is a carrier-neutral plug-in that continuously identifies electromechanical dynamics and constrains adaptive piezo control; existing products chiefly provide full LLRF stacks or project-specific fixed algorithms.
ranked_candidates.timing_window_risk: Labs may keep the algorithm entirely in-house, Libera may add equivalent adaptive identification, or each cavity family may need too much custom engineering for product economics. Kill if the algorithm fails to transfer across two cavity classes, cannot coexist with existing interlocks, or no lab accepts a paid evaluation by end-2029.
ranked_candidates.commercial_readiness_kill_date: 2034; commercial kill at end-2029 without a paid lab evaluation or signed procurement path
ranked_candidates.extreme_edge: Automatically identify a cavity's changing mechanical plant and retune a constrained piezo waveform in minutes, aiming for 10x peak-detuning suppression without destabilizing a high-Q resonator.
ranked_candidates.first_experiment: 2027-2028, 12 months: implement the daughtercard against 325 and 650 MHz real-time cavity emulators, then one accessible SRF cavity/test stand. Across thermal/microphonic conditions, identify dominant modes within five minutes and suppress peak detuning at least 10x versus no compensation and at least 5x versus fixed feedforward, while reducing peak forward-RF overhead by >=20% and triggering the safety fallback for every injected unstable mode. Kill if transfer requires manual code changes per cavity, an unsafe mode escapes the guard, or the 5x fixed-feedforward delta is not reproduced independently.
ranked_candidates.design_in_or_procurement_engagement_path: 2028 SBIR/CRADA or paid test-stand evaluation; 2029 signed Common Platform/MTCA.4 interface commitment, paid qualification, or spares/commissioning work package. A scientific collaboration without a commercial path does not count.
ranked_candidates.safety_regulatory_export_path: The card remains subordinate to independent machine-protection and RF interlocks; adaptive outputs have hard amplitude/slew/energy limits, watchdog fallback, configuration signatures, and operator override. US DOE civilian accelerator use is the base case. Export classification and end-use screening precede any foreign quote.
ranked_candidates.founder_fit_note: FPGA signal processing, system identification, feedback control, RF instrumentation, embedded safety, and test automation fit generic EE/CE capability; SRF cryomodule operation and machine protection require laboratory domain partners.

G1.rationale: Independent Fermilab and BNL primary documents describe exact LLRF/SRF control problems and active hardware work; CD-3B records ordered chassis and funded build context.

G2.rationale: Six technical works are final peer-reviewed journal articles with DOI/publisher evidence; the BNL technical notes are typed as national-lab records, not academic quota.

G3.rationale: The 12-month $145k emulator-plus-cavity experiment has transfer, suppression, RF-overhead, safety, and buyer kills.

G4.rationale: BNL/JLab, Fermilab/SLAC, Libera LLRF, KEK, and MTCA.4 incumbents are named; the plug-in online electromechanical identification and constrained adaptive piezo layer is architecturally distinct from a full LLRF replacement.

G5.rationale: Adaptive detuning compensation, real-time cavity simulation, and system identification are peer-demonstrated; the experiment tests portability and safe integration.

G6.rationale: Independent machine protection, hard output constraints, watchdog fallback, configuration control, US civilian base case, and export screening are explicit.

G7.rationale: Bounded preparation, PIP-II 2028 completion/commissioning, EIC 2030-2034 RF integration, ordered hardware, launch TRL, in-house absorption risk, and kill dates are explicit.

demonstrated_demand.evidence: Fermilab documents the exact instability/calibration pain and BNL documents active EIC platform deployment.

frontier_coolness_vision.evidence: Self-characterizing SRF cavities are a compelling control-platform advance.

high_end_niche_quality.evidence: Small buyer set, high system value, repeat commissioning and spares.

competition_whitespace.evidence: Powerful in-house teams and Libera constrain the socket.

technical_elegance_controllability.evidence: The plant, disturbances, outputs, guards, and failure modes are measurable in real time.

tenx_technical_edge.evidence: 10x detuning suppression is testable but not yet portable across cavity families.

us_china_dual_market_leverage.evidence: Strong US national-lab beachhead; no China claim.

launch_window_fit_2030.evidence: PIP-II commissioning and EIC integration overlap the launch window.

expansion_economics.evidence: Expansion to FELs, light sources, and industrial SRF is plausible but expert-service-heavy.

founder_skill_transfer.evidence: Core product is FPGA/RF instrumentation, identification, feedback, and embedded safety.

ranked_candidates.distinctness_check: New L05 control daughtercard; not a relabel of the D-19 desalination product, A-02 breaker, A-21 plasma-remediation product, A-22 PFAS destruction, C-09 pulsed-power platform, D-09 beam-dose metrology, F-02 magnet balance-of-plant, or F-20 high-voltage modules.
